name: Certified interpolation and neutral completions add-on v12
freeze_scope: Recorded before executing the v12 evaluations, after inspecting the v11 results (including the PL advantage on the original smooth family); this is not preregistration.
selection: All eight original inputs, both grids, both policies, both weight profiles and all three alpha values; no outcome-based exclusions.
anchoring: Triangular, minimax, sweep and piecewise-linear plans are the archived v11 selections; PL is recomputed and asserted identical.
certified_interpolation: CI-tau: among eligible plans whose upper objective J+ is at most (1+tau) times the minimax value on the same grid and policy, choose the plan minimizing the PL objective; ties by workload, maximum upper risk and enumeration index. tau in {0, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10}. tau=0 is minimax with a PL tie-break; tau large recovers PL.
neutral_family: For every leg and every interval between adjacent full-grid endpoints, an independent exponent drawn log-uniformly on [0.1, 10] (symmetric around one on a log scale, same range as the v11 stress powers) defines q_lo-(q_lo-q_hi)*z**exponent. Every draw preserves all full-grid endpoints and is therefore an admissible completion for both grids. Thirty draws per input; numpy default_rng seed 20261027 plus input index.
evaluation: Regret is the test objective minus the exact test optimum on the identical grid/policy feasible set, as in v11. Families are reported separately: original smooth (0.45, 1, 2.2), stress (0.1, 10), neutral (30 draws). The common least-favourable completion yields the robust gap, reported as a deterministic certificate.
primary_outputs: Main table: Tri., MM, Sweep, PL, CI-0.02, CI-0.05 on the four-level uncapped and capped domains with robust gap, smooth regret and neutral regret; supplementary table for all tau, grids and policies; frontier figure.
limitations: Constructed memberships and completion families are not calibrated operational uncertainty.
The neutral family is one choice of an uninformative distribution over admissible completions, not an empirical distribution.
Repeated settings are descriptive and not independent replications.
